findings.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:20 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied uniformly to both the ready-topic branch and the "loading" placeholder branch, so the loading page can get cached and served for a minute even after the topic becomes ready

app/models/topic_embed.rb:14 — TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create on `embed_url` (`where(embed_url: url).first` then `create!`), so two concurrent imports of the same new URL race and the loser hits an unhandled unique-index violation

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:19 — feed_key` is computed (SHA1 of the feed URL) but never referenced anywhere else in the job, so the apparent "skip if feed unchanged" throttling is not actually implemented

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — Switching to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` introduces an unrescued network fetch inside the per-thread import loop, so a single failing URL now raises and aborts the entire disqus import batch instead of just that thread

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 — RSS/Atom feed content is imported via `TopicEmbed.import` with `cook_method: raw_html` and rendered unsanitized, so a compromised or malicious feed at the admin-configured `feed_polling_url` can inject stored XSS served to every visitor of the topic

app/models/post.rb:63 — Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (bypassing the sanitize/cook pipeline) whenever `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so any HTML in imported content is rendered to anonymous, unauthenticated visitors with no sanitization

lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — Host is validated once against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` via `URI(@embed_url).host`, but the subsequent `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb:48) follows HTTP redirects unchecked, so the validated host can redirect the server to fetch an arbitrary/internal URL (TOCTOU/SSRF)

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is set whenever `ensure_embeddable` passes, but that check relies solely on the client-controlled, spoofable `Referer` header, so the frame-embedding permission (and everything gated behind it) can be granted to any raw HTTP client regardless of actual page context
app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — skip_validations: true` on `PostCreator.new` for imported posts removes normal model-level defense-in-depth validation for attacker/feed-influenced content

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no URL-scheme allowlist (e.g. could be `file://` depending on open-uri version/config), relying entirely on admin trust of the configured feed URL
lib/topic_retriever.rb:23 — The raw, attacker-supplied `@embed_url` string is interpolated directly into the Redis key (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`) with no length bound or sanitization

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:15 — discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a weak substring-based postMessage origin check rather than exact-match, so an origin merely containing `discourseUrl` as a substring could pass
lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — Removing the `--category`/`-c` CLI option is a breaking change for any existing scripts/automation that invoke `disqus.thor import` with `-c`/`--category

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:20 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` caches a response whose body varies by `current_user` (passed into `TopicView.new`) and by whether the topic exists yet, risking a cached personalized/stale response being served to a different embedding visitor

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:12 — params.require(:embed_url)` raises an unhandled `ActionController::ParameterMissing` with no explicit rescue/response shape, leaving the embeddable contract's error behavior for missing params undefined for third-party integrators

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:8 — The embed script hardcodes the unversioned path `embed/best`, so any future breaking change to this route has no version namespace to evolve into without breaking every third-party site that already embedded the old `embed.js

config/routes.rb:245 — The new `embed/best` route has no format/version constraints, leaving the externally-consumed contract (used by arbitrary third-party embedding sites) unconstrained and harder to evolve safely later

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (and the feed fetch in poll_feed.rb:29) specifies no read/open timeout, so a slow or non-responding remote server can hang the job worker indefinitely

lib/topic_retriever.rb:1 — TopicRetriever#retrieve`/`perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` have no exception handling around the network fetch or import calls, so any network error, parse error, or ActiveRecord error propagates up and fails the enclosing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job with no graceful degradation

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32 — The `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` loop has no per-item rescue, so one malformed/failing feed item aborts processing of all remaining items in that run

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14 — Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` is fired on every cache-miss request from an unauthenticated public controller action with no rate limiting at the controller level, only later inside the job via a 60s redis throttle

lib/topic_retriever.rb:34 — perform_retrieve` synchronously instantiates and calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly (bypassing the job queue) from inside a different job/service, coupling job lifecycles and defeating the purpose of `Jobs::PollFeed` being a separately scheduled/queued job

lib/topic_retriever.rb:22 — The redis `setnx` + `expire` pair is not atomic, so a crash or delay between the two calls could leave the throttle key without an expiry (or, on setnx failure, no expiry is set at all in that path)

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:39 — The success-path specs stub `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` directly, but production code in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14 goes through `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` → `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9), so the test never actually exercises or validates that integration path

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — Jobs::RetrieveTopic` has no dedicated spec at all — argument validation (`InvalidParameters`), user lookup, and the `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` staff-bypass logic are all untested
app/models/topic_embed.rb:38 — TopicEmbed.import_remote` (the readability-based fetch/parse path actually used in production for controller-triggered retrieval) has no test coverage at all
app/models/topic_embed.rb:56 — absolutize_urls` edge cases (https vs http, non-default ports, malformed/absolute hrefs) are untested; existing spec only covers one simple relative-path case

lib/topic_retriever.rb:22 — TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`'s real redis throttle behavior is always stubbed (`.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(...)`) rather than tested against actual redis setnx/expire behavior
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:23 — Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the actual RSS parsing/import loop, has zero test coverage — the spec only covers the guard-clause conditions in `#execute

app/models/post.rb:63 — The new `cook_method: :raw_html` behavior, which renders raw HTML unsanitized via `raw post.cooked` in the embed view, has no regression test guarding against future accidental sanitization/XSS exposure changes

app/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:7 — The "is 404 without an embed_url" test title claims 404 but only asserts `response.should_not be_success`, which doesn't actually verify the status code is 404 specifically

app/models/topic_embed.rb:56 — absolutize_urls` duplicates the identical rewrite loop for `a[href]` and `img[src]`, differing only in attribute name, and could be collapsed into one parameterized loop
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:19 — feed_key` is dead code — defined but never called anywhere in the diff

lib/topic_retriever.rb:34 — TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` synchronously instantiates and calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly, coupling two independently-scheduled job classes together rather than going through the job queue

lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — Host-validation logic (`URI(...).host` compared to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) is duplicated between `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` instead of being shared

app/models/topic_embed.rb:9 — TopicEmbed.import` mixes multiple concerns (content-sha diffing, post creation, post revision, embed bookkeeping) in one class method, making it harder to test and extend in isolation

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — A pre-existing, already-shipped migration was edited in place to add `force: true`; on any environment where `top_topics` already exists, replaying/rerunning migrations from scratch would now silently drop and recreate the table (data loss), and editing an already-run migration's DDL violates migration immutability

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Adds a `NOT NULL` column with a default directly to the `posts` table (potentially large in production installs) in a single step, which can trigger a full table rewrite/lock on older Postgres/MySQL versions instead of using a backfill-then-constrain pattern

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true` on a brand-new `create_table` is low risk (informational) since the table shouldn't already exist, but would silently drop it if it unexpectedly does

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — ensure_embeddable` authorizes solely on `request.referer`, an HTTP header any raw client (curl, script, non-browser attacker) fully controls and can spoof to exactly `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, making the only access gate on this unauthenticated, iframe-embeddable endpoint trivially bypassable so anyone can drive the fetch/import pipeline directly without ever loading a real embedding page

app/models/post.rb:69 — cook` returns `raw` unsanitized for `cook_method: raw_html`, and combined with `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` (`raw post.cooked`) and `app/models/topic_embed.rb:38` (readability's `attributes: %w[href src]` allowlist preserves `href`/`src` verbatim with no scheme filtering), an `<a href="javascript:...">` in fetched content survives `absolutize_urls` (only rewrites hrefs starting with `/`) and is rendered as live unescaped HTML in a real forum topic, giving stored XSS to anyone who can place such a tag in content served from embeddable_host

app/models/topic_embed.rb:9 — return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\// ` in `import` runs only after `import_remote` (topic_embed.rb:38) has already performed `open(url).read` against the attacker-supplied `embed_url`, so the scheme allowlist is applied too late to prevent the outbound fetch itself

lib/topic_retriever.rb:24 — Both the redis throttle key (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`) and the `TopicEmbed` dedup lookup (app/models/topic_embed.rb:14) key on the raw, unnormalized embed_url string, so an attacker can bypass the 60s throttle and force unlimited distinct fetch+import cycles simply by varying the query string/fragment of an otherwise-identical URL

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14 — Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` fires unconditionally on every cache-miss request with no rate limiting on the controller action itself, so combined with the per-string throttle bypass above, an unauthenticated caller can flood the job queue and trigger unbounded outbound HTTP fetches and Topic creation

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:16 — no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` bypasses the 60s throttle whenever the triggering request's `current_user` is staff; combined with `PostRevisor.revise!(..., bypass_rate_limiter: true)`, a staff member's ordinary browser load under attacker influence lets an attacker force rapid repeated re-imports/revisions with no rate limiting at all

app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — absolutize_urls` only rewrites `href`/`src` values that `start_with?('/')`; protocol-relative (`//evil.com/...`), `data:`, and other absolute-but-not-leading-slash URIs pass through completely untouched into a real forum post rendered unsanitized

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:20 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied uniformly to both the ready-topic branch and the "loading" placeholder branch, so the loading page can get cached and served for a minute even after the topic becomes ready

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after the `if topic_id ... else render 'loading'` branch, so the `loading` response will carry the same cache headers as the fully-rendered response. If `discourse_expires_in` results in client/proxy caching for that duration, a user may keep receiving the cached loading page for up to a minute even after the background job creates the embed/topic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:14 — TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create on `embed_url` (`where(embed_url: url).first` then `create!`), so two concurrent imports of the same new URL race and the loser hits an unhandled unique-index violation

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, it first does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, when blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. Because `topic_embeds.embed_url` has a unique index (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`), two concurrent imports of the same new URL can both observe no row and then race to `create!`; the loser will raise an unrescued uniqueness violation (e.g., `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`). The diff shows no exception handling or atomic upsert pattern to avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:19 — feed_key` is computed (SHA1 of the feed URL) but never referenced anywhere else in the job, so the apparent "skip if feed unchanged" throttling is not actually implemented

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined (SHA1 of `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but is never called anywhere in the job. The actual polling logic in `poll_feed` always fetches/parses the feed via `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` with no check against a stored/previous value, so any intended “skip if unchanged” behavior is not implemented (this is dead/incomplete code rather than a directly broken behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — Switching to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` introduces an unrescued network fetch inside the per-thread import loop, so a single failing URL now raises and aborts the entire disqus import batch instead of just that thread

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Disqus import loop to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` (lib/tasks/disqus.thor), and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) with no rescue. Since the per-thread loop also has no exception handling, a single network/HTTP failure (e.g., OpenURI::HTTPError, timeout) will raise and abort the entire batch, whereas the previous implementation just created a post containing the permalink and did not depend on a live fetch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 — RSS/Atom feed content is imported via `TopicEmbed.import` with `cook_method: raw_html` and rendered unsanitized, so a compromised or malicious feed at the admin-configured `feed_polling_url` can inject stored XSS served to every visitor of the topic

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed items are parsed and `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is passed directly to `TopicEmbed.import`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the created post uses `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, explicitly skipping the rendering/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then outputs it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This diff therefore introduces a path where HTML from an admin-configured feed can be stored and served unsanitized, enabling stored XSS if that feed content is malicious/compromised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:63 — Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (bypassing the sanitize/cook pipeline) whenever `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so any HTML in imported content is rendered to anonymous, unauthenticated visitors with no sanitization

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook` + filters) entirely. The new RSS/import path explicitly sets this mode: `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, where `contents` comes from feed/remote HTML (`SimpleRSS.parse ... i.content`, `Readability::Document#content`) and is not sanitized in this diff. The embed views render `raw post.cooked`, so any HTML in imported content would be served directly, including to unauthenticated embed consumers, without sanitization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — Host is validated once against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` via `URI(@embed_url).host`, but the subsequent `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb:48) follows HTTP redirects unchecked, so the validated host can redirect the server to fetch an arbitrary/internal URL (TOCTOU/SSRF)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` which only checks the initial `@embed_url` host via `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). However, retrieval ultimately calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) with no redirect ограничения; `open-uri` can follow HTTP redirects, so an allowed-host URL can redirect the server to fetch content from a different (potentially internal/arbitrary) host, creating an SSRF vector despite the prior host check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is set whenever `ensure_embeddable` passes, but that check relies solely on the client-controlled, spoofable `Referer` header, so the frame-embedding permission (and everything gated behind it) can be granted to any raw HTTP client regardless of actual page context
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the controller sets `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`, disabling clickjacking protection, and that the gating check relies on the client-controlled/spoofable `Referer` header, allowing bypass—matching the core golden issue. It doesn’t explicitly mention the nil-referer-to-empty-string fallback masking failures, but it identifies the same underlying vulnerability and bypass mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — skip_validations: true` on `PostCreator.new` for imported posts removes normal model-level defense-in-depth validation for attacker/feed-influenced content

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly creates imported posts with `PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` in `TopicEmbed.import`, and updates them with `PostRevisor#revise!` passing `skip_validations: true` as well. The diff also changes `PostRevisor` to honor this flag via `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, confirming validations are actually bypassed. Because imported content is feed/remote-URL influenced (see `Jobs::PollFeed` and `import_remote`), skipping model validations removes normal defense-in-depth checks for attacker-controlled input, making this a verifiable security/correctness issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no URL-scheme allowlist (e.g. could be `file://` depending on open-uri version/config), relying entirely on admin trust of the configured feed URL
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that PollFeed uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without sufficient validation/allowlisting of the configured URL, enabling fetching arbitrary resources (including internal/external URLs and potentially `file://`), i.e., an SSRF-style issue controlled via the site setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:23 — The raw, attacker-supplied `@embed_url` string is interpolated directly into the Redis key (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`) with no length bound or sanitization

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `retrieved_recently?` constructs `retrieved_key = "retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` directly from `@embed_url`, which ultimately comes from `params[:embed_url]` (EmbedController#best enqueues it unchanged). While `invalid_host?` checks that `URI(@embed_url).host` matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, it does not constrain the overall URL length or normalize it. An attacker can supply an extremely long but valid URL on the allowed host, causing very large Redis keys and potential resource/DoS issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:15 — discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a weak substring-based postMessage origin check rather than exact-match, so an origin merely containing `discourseUrl` as a substring could pass
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: using indexOf/substring logic for postMessage origin validation allows malicious origins that include the trusted discourseUrl as part of their domain (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com) to bypass the check, instead of requiring an exact origin match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — Removing the `--category`/`-c` CLI option is a breaking change for any existing scripts/automation that invoke `disqus.thor import` with `-c`/`--category

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Thor option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the associated `category_id` lookup and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. Any existing automation invoking `disqus.thor import -c/--category ...` would now error with an unknown option, which is a backward-incompatible CLI change, but not a correctness defect in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:20 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` caches a response whose body varies by `current_user` (passed into `TopicView.new`) and by whether the topic exists yet, risking a cached personalized/stale response being served to a different embedding visitor

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the rendered body depends on (a) whether `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns a topic yet (renders `loading` vs building `@topic_view`), and (b) it passes `current_user` into `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`, which can make the output user-dependent. The diff also adds `discourse_expires_in 1.minute`, which sets caching headers for this action. The diff alone doesn’t show whether that caching is private/per-user or shared/public, so the “served to a different visitor” impact can’t be proven here, but the concern about stale/personalized caching is diff-grounded and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:12 — params.require(:embed_url)` raises an unhandled `ActionController::ParameterMissing` with no explicit rescue/response shape, leaving the embeddable contract's error behavior for missing params undefined for third-party integrators

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best the line `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when the param is absent, and there is no local `rescue`/explicit response for that case in this controller. The spec (`it "is 404 without an embed_url" do get :best; response.should_not be_success end`) only asserts non-success and does not define a specific status/body contract. This is a real, diff-grounded concern about the embed endpoint’s externally consumed error behavior, but it’s not clearly a functional defect since Rails’ default handling may be acceptable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:8 — The embed script hardcodes the unversioned path `embed/best`, so any future breaking change to this route has no version namespace to evolve into without breaking every third-party site that already embedded the old `embed.js

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` sets `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`, and `config/routes.rb` adds the matching unversioned route `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'`. This is not a functional defect in the PR, but it is a concrete forward-compatibility/API-evolution concern: third-party embeds will be tightly coupled to this path with no version namespace.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:245 — The new `embed/best` route has no format/version constraints, leaving the externally-consumed contract (used by arbitrary third-party embedding sites) unconstrained and harder to evolve safely later

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an externally used route `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` in `config/routes.rb` with no constraints/defaults (e.g., `defaults: { format: :html }` or versioning/namespace). While this is not a functional defect by itself (the controller renders HTML views), it does leave the public embedding endpoint contract unconstrained, which can make future evolution (formats/versions) harder and is a reasonable architecture/API-surface review concern grounded in the added route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (and the feed fetch in poll_feed.rb:29) specifies no read/open timeout, so a slow or non-responding remote server can hang the job worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds network fetches using `open-uri` without any explicit timeout options: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb` (import_remote). While the claim of "indefinitely" depends on Ruby/Net::HTTP defaults and can’t be proven from the diff alone, it’s a real, diff-grounded operational concern that these jobs may block for an unbounded/too-long period on slow or stuck remote servers unless timeouts are set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:1 — TopicRetriever#retrieve`/`perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` have no exception handling around the network fetch or import calls, so any network error, parse error, or ActiveRecord error propagates up and fails the enclosing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job with no graceful degradation

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`, and `import_remote` does `open(url).read` and then runs parsing/import logic (`Readability::Document.new`, `TopicEmbed.import`, `PostCreator#create`, `TopicEmbed.create!`, etc.) without any `rescue`. `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` similarly does not rescue around `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. So network/parse/DB exceptions will indeed propagate and fail the job. However, this is primarily a robustness/operational concern (how failures should be handled/retried/logged) rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32 — The `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` loop has no per-item rescue, so one malformed/failing feed item aborts processing of all remaining items in that run

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the new `poll_feed` method iterates `rss.items.each` and does parsing/transformation (`i.link`, `i.content.scrub`, `CGI.unescapeHTML`, `TopicEmbed.import`) without any per-item `rescue`. In Ruby, an exception in any iteration will abort the method and stop processing remaining items for that run (and `sidekiq_options retry: false` makes this more impactful). This is a real robustness/edge-case concern grounded in the diff, but it’s not provably a defect without an explicit requirement to continue on malformed items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14 — Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` is fired on every cache-miss request from an unauthenticated public controller action with no rate limiting at the controller level, only later inside the job via a 60s redis throttle

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, the action unconditionally calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). There is no controller-side throttling or deduping, and the action appears publicly callable (no auth filter; only `ensure_embeddable` checks `request.referer` host). The only shown throttle is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (60s Redis key) which prevents *work* but does not prevent repeated job enqueues, so repeated requests can still flood Sidekiq with no-op jobs. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/DoS risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:34 — perform_retrieve` synchronously instantiates and calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly (bypassing the job queue) from inside a different job/service, coupling job lifecycles and defeating the purpose of `Jobs::PollFeed` being a separately scheduled/queued job

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` directly runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, instead of enqueueing it (e.g., via `Jobs.enqueue`). This is verifiably synchronous invocation of a scheduled job class from inside a different service flow, increasing coupling and bypassing Sidekiq/job-queue semantics (retry, isolation, scheduling intent), even though it will still function correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:22 — The redis `setnx` + `expire` pair is not atomic, so a crash or delay between the two calls could leave the throttle key without an expiry (or, on setnx failure, no expiry is set at all in that path)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands; if the process crashes or is interrupted after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key can be left without a TTL, causing the embed URL to be throttled indefinitely. This is a real correctness/behavior defect introduced by the diff’s throttling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:39 — The success-path specs stub `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` directly, but production code in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14 goes through `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` → `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9), so the test never actually exercises or validates that integration path

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best, when no topic_id is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and does not directly instantiate `TopicRetriever`. However spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb (the "tells the topic retriever" example) expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`. This means the spec is not aligned with the controller’s actual behavior and also doesn’t validate the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` integration path introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — Jobs::RetrieveTopic` has no dedicated spec at all — argument validation (`InvalidParameters`), user lookup, and the `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` staff-bypass logic are all untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new job `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` with nontrivial behavior: it raises `Discourse::InvalidParameters` when `args[:embed_url]` is missing, conditionally looks up a `User` by `args[:user_id]`, and passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. In the added specs (`spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) there is no spec covering `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, so these behaviors are indeed untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:38 — TopicEmbed.import_remote` (the readability-based fetch/parse path actually used in production for controller-triggered retrieval) has no test coverage at all

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (uses `open(url).read` and `Readability::Document` to parse HTML and then calls `TopicEmbed.import`). This path is invoked by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (used by the controller-triggered retrieval flow) and by `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`. However, the added specs only cover `TopicEmbed.import` (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) and do not exercise `import_remote` at all, so the new readability/network parsing logic lacks direct test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56 — absolutize_urls` edge cases (https vs http, non-default ports, malformed/absolute hrefs) are untested; existing spec only covers one simple relative-path case

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new nontrivial URL-rewriting logic in `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` (parses `URI(url)`, builds a `prefix` with scheme/host and optional non-default port, and rewrites only `href`/`src` values that start with `/`). The added spec (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) asserts only one basic http + leading-slash relative link/image case. It does not cover other realistic cases implied by the implementation and comment (https vs http, non-default ports, already-absolute URLs, protocol-relative URLs, relative paths without leading `/`, malformed `href/src`). This is a concrete test coverage gap for new behavior, not a directly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:22 — TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`'s real redis throttle behavior is always stubbed (`.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(...)`) rather than tested against actual redis setnx/expire behavior

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `retrieved_recently?` contains nontrivial throttling logic using `$redis.setnx` and `$redis.expire` (lines within the new method). However, in spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb the tests for calling `perform_retrieve` explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false (`topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)`), so the real Redis-based throttle behavior is never exercised by the spec. This is a concrete test coverage gap for newly added logic, not an application defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:23 — Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the actual RSS parsing/import loop, has zero test coverage — the spec only covers the guard-clause conditions in `#execute

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial logic in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb#poll_feed`: it fetches `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` via `open-uri`, parses with `SimpleRSS.parse`, normalizes item URLs, unescapes/scrubs content, and calls `TopicEmbed.import` in a loop. The accompanying spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only verifies `#execute` guard conditions and that `#poll_feed` is invoked, but contains no tests covering the parsing/import behavior inside `#poll_feed` itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:63 — The new `cook_method: :raw_html` behavior, which renders raw HTML unsanitized via `raw post.cooked` in the embed view, has no regression test guarding against future accidental sanitization/XSS exposure changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* add a regression test covering the new `cook_method == :raw_html` behavior: `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` asserts `post.cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and, critically, `post.cooked.should == post.raw`, which would fail if future changes accidentally sanitized or altered the HTML. The embed view’s `raw post.cooked` is exercised indirectly by this invariance (cooked==raw) and by the URL-absolutization assertion including ``/`` HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:7 — The "is 404 without an embed_url" test title claims 404 but only asserts `response.should_not be_success`, which doesn't actually verify the status code is 404 specifically

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the example `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do` only does `get :best` followed by `response.should_not be_success`, which does not assert a 404 status specifically (it would pass for any non-success like 400/500). The title claims 404, so the test is imprecise/misleading and doesn’t verify the intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56 — absolutize_urls` duplicates the identical rewrite loop for `a[href]` and `img[src]`, differing only in attribute name, and could be collapsed into one parameterized loop

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls the diff does show two very similar loops (one over `fragment.css('a')` rewriting `href`, and one over `fragment.css('img')` rewriting `src`). However, this is a refactor/DRY suggestion about code duplication, not a defect or substantive review issue grounded in correctness/security/behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:19 — feed_key` is dead code — defined but never called anywhere in the diff

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined (memoizing a Redis key based on `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but there are no references to `feed_key` anywhere else in the diff, including within `poll_feed`/`execute`. This makes it dead/unused code in the current change, which is a maintainability issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:34 — TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` synchronously instantiates and calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly, coupling two independently-scheduled job classes together rather than going through the job queue

adjudication.rationale: Verified in lib/topic_retriever.rb within `perform_retrieve`: when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, it directly runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (synchronously) before falling back to `fetch_http`. This couples the scheduled job class (`Jobs::PollFeed < Jobs::Scheduled`) to an on-demand retrieval path rather than enqueueing work via the job system, which is an architectural/scope concern but not a clear functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — Host-validation logic (`URI(...).host` compared to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) is duplicated between `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` instead of being shared

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate implementations of embeddable-host validation: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` raises unless `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is present and `URI(request.referer || '').host` matches it, while `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` independently checks `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` (with its own URI error handling). This is real duplication introduced by the change and is a maintainability/consistency concern rather than an immediate functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:9 — TopicEmbed.import` mixes multiple concerns (content-sha diffing, post creation, post revision, embed bookkeeping) in one class method, making it harder to test and extend in isolation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import` as a large class method that handles multiple responsibilities in one place: mutating/annotating contents (`contents << ...`), computing diffing state (`content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` and comparing to `embed.content_sha1`), creating posts/topics in a transaction via `PostCreator`, revising existing posts via `PostRevisor`, and maintaining embed bookkeeping (`TopicEmbed.create!`, `embed.update_column`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/architecture concern (harder to test/extend in isolation), not a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — A pre-existing, already-shipped migration was edited in place to add `force: true`; on any environment where `top_topics` already exists, replaying/rerunning migrations from scratch would now silently drop and recreate the table (data loss), and editing an already-run migration's DDL violates migration immutability

adjudication.rationale: The diff does edit an existing migration in place: `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` changes `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. Editing already-merged/previously-run migrations is generally considered unsafe/immutable history. While the finding’s “replaying from scratch” data-loss scenario is overstated (a true from-scratch migrate typically runs on an empty DB), `force: true` would drop the table if this migration were ever re-executed against a DB where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., migration redo/reset workflows), so the concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Adds a `NOT NULL` column with a default directly to the `posts` table (potentially large in production installs) in a single step, which can trigger a full table rewrite/lock on older Postgres/MySQL versions instead of using a backfill-then-constrain pattern

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` that does `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` in a single step. On large `posts` tables, adding a NOT NULL column with a DEFAULT can cause a table rewrite and/or long lock on some DBs/versions, so the review concern is valid as an operational/migration-risk issue rather than an application correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true` on a brand-new `create_table` is low risk (informational) since the table shouldn't already exist, but would silently drop it if it unexpectedly does

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` does use `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. On a new table this is usually unnecessary; if the table already exists for any reason, `force: true` will drop/recreate it (potentially losing data) rather than failing loudly. This is a real, diff-grounded review concern but not a definite defect in normal fresh migrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — ensure_embeddable` authorizes solely on `request.referer`, an HTTP header any raw client (curl, script, non-browser attacker) fully controls and can spoof to exactly `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, making the only access gate on this unauthenticated, iframe-embeddable endpoint trivially bypassable so anyone can drive the fetch/import pipeline directly without ever loading a real embedding page

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` gates access by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), but `Referer` is a client-controlled header and can be spoofed by non-browser clients. Since `/embed/best` is otherwise unauthenticated and will enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` when no topic exists, a caller can bypass the only check by setting a matching Referer and drive the fetch/import pipeline without actually embedding the page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:69 — cook` returns `raw` unsanitized for `cook_method: raw_html`, and combined with `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` (`raw post.cooked`) and `app/models/topic_embed.rb:38` (readability's `attributes: %w[href src]` allowlist preserves `href`/`src` verbatim with no scheme filtering), an `<a href="javascript:...">` in fetched content survives `absolutize_urls` (only rewrites hrefs starting with `/`) and is rendered as live unescaped HTML in a real forum topic, giving stored XSS to anyone who can place such a tag in content served from embeddable_host

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `cook_method: :raw_html` path where `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (app/models/post.rb) and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: raw_html` from remotely fetched/feed HTML (app/models/topic_embed.rb). `absolutize_urls` only rewrites `href`/`src` values that start with `/`, so `href="javascript:..."` is preserved. `import_remote` uses Readability with an attributes allowlist including `href`/`src` but does not show any scheme filtering/sanitization in this diff. The embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), and these posts are also real topics/posts in the DB, so the raw HTML can become stored XSS for any viewer if the embedded/fetched content contains malicious attributes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:9 — return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\// ` in `import` runs only after `import_remote` (topic_embed.rb:38) has already performed `open(url).read` against the attacker-supplied `embed_url`, so the scheme allowlist is applied too late to prevent the outbound fetch itself

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `open(url).read` before calling `TopicEmbed.import`. The scheme allowlist (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`) exists only in `import`, so it cannot prevent the outbound fetch that already occurred. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only checks `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and does not restrict scheme, so a non-HTTP scheme like `ftp://<allowed-host>/...` could pass the host check and still trigger `open(url).read`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:24 — Both the redis throttle key (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`) and the `TopicEmbed` dedup lookup (app/models/topic_embed.rb:14) key on the raw, unnormalized embed_url string, so an attacker can bypass the 60s throttle and force unlimited distinct fetch+import cycles simply by varying the query string/fragment of an otherwise-identical URL

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` builds the throttle key from the raw string (`retrieved_key = "retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`), and `perform_retrieve` / `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` / `TopicEmbed.import` dedup by exact-match `embed_url` (`where(embed_url: @embed_url)` / `where(embed_url: url)`). There is no normalization/canonicalization of URLs anywhere in the added code, and `invalid_host?` only checks `URI(@embed_url).host`, so the same host with different query string/fragment will be treated as distinct for both throttling and dedup, allowing repeated fetch/import cycles by varying the URL string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14 — Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` fires unconditionally on every cache-miss request with no rate limiting on the controller action itself, so combined with the per-string throttle bypass above, an unauthenticated caller can flood the job queue and trigger unbounded outbound HTTP fetches and Topic creation

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, the action always enqueues `:retrieve_topic` (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`) with no controller-level rate limiting. Access is not gated by authentication (no `require_login`), and `ensure_embeddable` only checks `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which can be spoofed by a client. The queued job runs `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, whose throttle key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (per-URL string), so an attacker can vary `embed_url` paths on the allowed host to bypass throttling and cause many jobs and outbound `open(url)` fetches (`TopicEmbed.import_remote`) and potentially unbounded topic creation (unique `topic_embeds.embed_url` allows infinite distinct URLs). This is a real queue-flooding / outbound-fetch / spam vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:16 — no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` bypasses the 60s throttle whenever the triggering request's `current_user` is staff; combined with `PostRevisor.revise!(..., bypass_rate_limiter: true)`, a staff member's ordinary browser load under attacker influence lets an attacker force rapid repeated re-imports/revisions with no rate limiting at all

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly bypasses the 60s retrieval throttle for staff-triggered requests: `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb), and `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` returns `false` immediately when `@opts[:no_throttle]` is set (lib/topic_retriever.rb), allowing unthrottled repeated fetches/import attempts. Additionally, on updates `TopicEmbed.import` calls `PostRevisor#revise!` with `bypass_rate_limiter: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), reinforcing that repeated revisions are intended to skip protections. While the exact rate-limiter behavior of `bypass_rate_limiter` isn't shown in this diff, the staff throttle bypass itself is verifiable and can enable rapid repeated imports/revisions when a staff browser triggers the endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — absolutize_urls` only rewrites `href`/`src` values that `start_with?('/')`; protocol-relative (`//evil.com/...`), `data:`, and other absolute-but-not-leading-slash URIs pass through completely untouched into a real forum post rendered unsanitized

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, imported HTML is saved with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for that method (skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline). The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (best.html.erb), so the HTML is effectively unsanitized. `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` only rewrites `href`/`src` values starting with `'/'` and does not validate or restrict URI schemes, so protocol-relative (`//...`), `data:`, `javascript:`, etc. pass through unchanged into rendered HTML. That is a concrete security/correctness defect exposed by this diff.
